user.title: How does Home Assistant reach your panel?
user.description:
Most people have a **SmartCom** (the box the Texecom app uses): choose **Texecom Connect**.

Choose **Crestron** only if one of the panel's COM ports is set to *Crestron System* and you reach it through a serial-to-network adapter or a cable.

connect.title: Your SmartCom
connect.description:
Find the SmartCom in your router's list of devices and reserve its address so it never changes.

Home Assistant uses the SmartCom's connection for the Texecom app, so the app can't connect while Home Assistant is: your alarm and the app's alarm notifications work as before. If Homebridge or texecom2mqtt use the SmartCom, turn them off first.

Connecting can take up to a minute.

arm_modes_crestron.title: Arm modes
arm_modes_crestron.description:
**'Away'** always arms the whole alarm. Choose the part arm behind **'Night'** and **'Home'**, or *'Not used'* to hide that button. Over Crestron, part arms work for area 1 only.

Crestron doesn't say whether the panel was fully or part armed when it's set at the keypad: choose how that should show.

panel_clock_wrong.title: Your alarm panel's clock is wrong

confirm.title: Set the panel's clock
confirm.description: The panel's clock is {drift}, usually because it lost all power (mains and battery). Its event log, and any timed arming your installer set up, use that clock.\n\nClick **Submit** to turn on **Keep the panel clock right**: Home Assistant sets the clock now, using its own time zone, and checks it once a day.
